explanation: A young shepherd and later king of Israel, known for his bravery and faith in God. He killed the giant Goliath in this story.
A large Philistine warrior, described as a giant, who was defeated by David in a duel.
A people who lived in Canaan, enemies of Israel during this period. Goliath was one of their foremost warriors.
The first king of Israel, who chose David to fight Goliath because of his faith and courage.
A musical instrument that David played to calm King Saul's mind.
The job David had before he became king; he tended his father's sheep.
The weapon David used to kill Goliath, a simple device that threw stones with great force and precision.
The army of the people of Israel, led by King Saul, which fought against the Philistine army.
A fight between two individuals, often representatives of each side in a conflict. David and Goliath met in such a contest.
Trust in and conviction about God's existence and power, something David demonstrated through his action against Goliath.
